# The Renewed Mind — Bill Johnson
Well, I am glad you showed up. Did anybody sleep good last night? I went into a coma myself. I don't know about you, but it was good.
They've done a scientific study recently, and they found that women who added a few extra pounds live longer than the men who mention it.
If liars' pants really did catch on fire, the news would be more fun to watch.
There's this cartoon I have to describe to you. All these animals are surrounding the manger, and they're all making their commitment of what they're going to do for the Christ child.
The camel says, "I will bear him gifts."
The donkey says, "I will carry him."
The fish says, "I will pay his taxes."
The cow says, "I will quench his thirst."
The dove says, "I will bless his baptism."
The sheep says, "I will warm him."
The duck says, "I will feed him."
The pig says, "I will let him fill me with demons and I'll jump off a cliff."
Oh, they get so funny.
Let me finish. The pig says, "I will let him fill me with demons and I'll jump off a cliff." And wait, what? Oh, goodness, so funny.
Well, I have one to read to you and then we'll get serious, I promise. This is an old one, so if you've heard it, just pretend like it's new. It's still one of my favorites.
As a bagpiper, I play many gigs. Recently, I was asked by a funeral director to play at a graveside service for a homeless man. He had no family or friends, so the service was to be at a pauper's cemetery in the Kentucky back country.
As I was not familiar with the backwoods, I got lost. And being a typical man, I didn't stop and get directions.
I finally arrived an hour late and saw the funeral guy had evidently gone, and the hearse was nowhere in sight. There were only the diggers and the crew left, and they were eating lunch. I felt badly and apologized to the men for being late.
I went to the graveside and looked down, and the vault lid was already in place. I didn't know what else to do, so I started to play.
The workers put down their lunches and began to gather around. I played my heart and soul out for this man with no family or friends. I played like I'd never played before for this homeless man.
And as I played "Amazing Grace," the workers began to weep. They wept, I wept, we all wept together.
When I finished, I packed up my bagpipes and started for my car. Though my head hung low, my heart was full.
As I was opening the door to my car, I heard one of the workers say, "Sweet mother of Jesus, I ain't never seen nothing like that before, and I've been putting in septic tanks for 20 years."
## The Renewed Mind
I want to talk to you about the renewed mind.
The most well-known verse and kind of the cornerstone verse on the renewed mind, at least that I'm familiar with, would be Romans 12:2.
"Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove the will of God, that which is good, acceptable, and perfect."
Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed. You and I are no more transformed in our lives than is our mind renewed.
The renewing of the mind is central to who we are and our assignment here on earth is actually to learn to live from the presence, from the reality of his world towards this one.
We are brokers of another world. We release presence, we release his purposes, we manifest his rule, his kingdom in situations.
And so he says, "Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove the will of God, that which is good, acceptable, and perfect."
I'd like to suggest to you that there's a number of ways for the miraculous realm to be released in our environments, and of course faith is absolutely central. Sometimes it's just through the manifestation of his presence. We see things happen that we never prayed for, never believed for. It just happens because he showed up.
And so there's a miracle realm that just comes in the presence. But I'd like to suggest to you that perhaps the most ignored realm that releases the miraculous is the renewed mind. Why? Because the renewed mind proves the will of God.
The renewed mind puts on display the will of God. What is the will of God? "On earth as it is in heaven. Your kingdom come, your will be done on earth as it is in heaven."
The renewed mind doesn't come just through the study of Scripture, and please don't take that as a put-down of Scripture, because that's the basis for everything. It's the Word of God that we learn, we get it into our heart.
But if the renewed mind came merely from the study of Scripture, the Pharisees would have had the most renewed minds on the planet. The devotion to Scripture itself was intense.
But Jesus said this in John 5:39. He said, "You search the Scriptures." He's talking to this group of Pharisees. "You search the Scriptures because you think in them is eternal life, but these testify of me and you're not willing to come to me."
So walk through this with me. You study the Scriptures because you think in them is eternal life. In other words, this is an end in itself.
He said, "These testify of me and you're unwilling to come to me." So, what's the point?
The printed word is to introduce you to the person of the Word.
It's to be the introduction to a divine encounter. It's the encounter that transforms us. It's the person.
You know what it's like to read the Scripture and have it come alive? What's happened? You're having an encounter with the one who inspired the book, who is the book.
People say there's errors in Scripture. I say no, there isn't. Then I say, "But for conversation's sake, let's just say there is." Then I'll say, "There's more errors in you than there is in this book, and I'm not going to let the greater error redefine the lesser."
People say, "Well, I don't remember what I read." Well, I don't remember what I had for lunch last Friday, either, but it still nourished me.
You just get it into you. You get it into you, but you learn. You know, we learn to recognize the person of Scripture.
He is the living Word, and to read and to have him introduce us to this one who thinks so completely different than all of us. And learning to think from his perspective is vital for us.
So, I want to take you just through a few of the biblical stories. So, if you'd open your Bibles to Mark chapter 4, and let's just start there and see how far we can get this morning.
As you see these stories, especially in the Gospels, as you go through the Scriptures just in your own reading of Scripture, look for where he thinks different. Look for where the renewed mind becomes manifest.
## Jesus and the Storm
Let's take this one story in Mark chapter 4. Let's read verse 35.
"On the same day, when evening had come, he said to them, 'Let us cross over to the other side.'
"Now, when they had left the multitude, they took him along in the boat as he was, and other little boats were also with him.
"And a great windstorm arose, and the waves beat into the boat so that it was already filling. But he was in the stern, asleep on a pillow. And they awoke him and said to him, 'Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?'
It's a great question to ask the Savior of the world.
Verse 39. "Then he arose and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, 'Peace, be still.' And the wind ceased, and there was great calm.
"And he said to them, 'Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?'
"And they feared exceedingly and said to one another, 'Who can this be that even the wind and the sea obey him?'"
Start with the last verse just to make a quick point. What fascinates me is when Jesus called his twelve disciples, he didn't give them a quiz to see who qualified to follow him.
And if there was any question that should be on the quiz, it should be, "Do you believe I'm the Messiah?" That's like a good starting place.
These guys actually followed him before they knew who he was. They belonged before they believed.
So, here's an interesting story. They're in a life-threatening storm again. And Jesus is sleeping.
I've heard people say he wasn't really sleeping. He was waiting for the disciples to come and get him. But the Bible says he was sleeping.
I believe the whole book, even the maps. Even the table of contents. I'm into the entire book.
And it says he was sleeping. He was sleeping. So, they woke him.
So, I hear other people say, "Well, he was sleeping because he was exhausted."
How about he was sleeping because the world he dwells in has no storms?
See, that when he says for us to abide in him, he modeled what that looked like. In fact, John chapter 3 gives us this most interesting statement where it says, I think it's verse 3, it says, "He who ascended."
Now, remember it's Jesus standing on planet Earth. He says, "He who ascended first descended. That is the Son of Man who is in heaven."
Where was Jesus? He was standing on planet Earth.
And he's telling his disciples, "I'm the one that descended, and as Son of Man I'm presently in heaven."
The Apostle Paul captured language for it when he said we were seated in Christ in heavenly places. We've actually been placed in a heavenly realm.
Now to live from there requires then a renewed mind. But it's what we have access to. We've heard it all week long. It's what we all have access to in Christ.
And so here is this fascinating story to me, and it shows me the renewed mind. Number one, Jesus slept in a storm. You have authority over any storm you can sleep in.
If you can find rest in the middle of chaos, you're positioned to really illustrate, demonstrate, manifest victory.
So they woke him up, and he rebukes the wind, the waves, it all calms down, and there's great peace.
Who's Jesus? He's the Son of God.
What do we call conversation with God? Prayer.
So the disciples came to God, and he answered their prayer and stilled the storm, and then asked them why they didn't have any faith.
That was a good point.
They gave him a request, a petition. He answered their prayer and then said, "How come you don't have any faith?"
They weren't being groomed to pray for miracles. They were being groomed to display miracles.
Most of what I have been taught through the years has been that I get into the middle of a problem and I cry out to God for him to come and repair and fix the problem. And when it happens, we give him praise. When it doesn't happen, we just blame it on the sovereignty of God.
Do you remember the young boy they brought to Jesus, or to the disciples, and they couldn't get him free?
And these, let's be honest, these guys had traveled with Jesus. He sent them out two by two.
These guys were the most trained in deliverance of anyone to ever live except for Jesus himself.
And when the child was brought to them, they couldn't bring deliverance to him. Jesus did with a word.
If that were to be done today and we couldn't bring deliverance or healing or whatever, we sweep it under the carpet called sovereignty of God.
And the disciples easily could have just said, "Well, this wasn't God's will. It wasn't God's timing."
But instead Jesus came to illustrate the standard of heaven that is supposed to be implemented, carried out here on earth by you and me.
And I don't always get it right. In fact, I get it wrong more times than I get it right. I'll be honest with you.
There's a lot of people that come to our place looking for a miracle. When they leave with a miracle, we give God the glory.
When they don't, I'm not going to do guilt and shame, but I am going to let that lack drive me into the presence to pray and to cry for greater breakthrough.
And this is how I pray. I say, "God, they came from the other side of the planet to meet with you, and all they met with was me, and neither of us are impressed."
We have the incredible privilege to represent Jesus well and to release into the earth what Jesus himself would release.
What is more powerful, the Word of God through the mouth of Jesus or the Word of God through your mouth?
It's the same. The power is in the Word.
Remember Jesus said that. He said, "I can do nothing of myself." He's the eternal Son of God. He has all power, access to everything, but he chose to restrict himself to the limitations of a man dependent on the Father.
So that he would give us an illustration that could actually be followed. Something that could be followed. Something that we could learn.
And so he restricted himself to the limitations of any person who was, number one, free from sin and, number two, empowered completely by the Holy Spirit.
And so we have those two qualifications. We're free from sin. Now we have to learn to be completely empowered by the Holy Spirit.
So this renewed mind, they come to Jesus and they wake him, he calms the storm on their behalf and then says, "How come you don't have any faith?"
There's a couple things that we need to learn out of this story. Number one is Jesus released peace over the storm. Why? Because he had it.
You can only give what you have.
Here's what it comes down to. This is what the renewed mind looks like. The renewed mind says that your internal reality will always become your external reality.
It's the reason maintaining peace here is so vital to protect our heart. Proverbs 4:23 has been a key verse for me for 50-some years. Watch over your heart with all diligence because from it flow the issues of life.
Be careful to watch the attitudes, the little tiny things that take place in the heart, the jealousies, the indifferences, whatever it might be, but we watch over those things as they creep up because it's out of that place flows the issues of life.
And you and I have been placed here to release the kingdom.
## The Word of God and the Kingdom
In John 1:14 it says Jesus is the Word of God made flesh. The Word of God made flesh, but in John chapter 6 he said the words that I speak to you are spirit and they are life.
So the Word of God became flesh, then became spirit.
I'm trying, man. I'm trying.
The Word of God, the word that I speak is spirit, and that spirit gives life.
So just think with me now. How is the kingdom of God manifest?
Many different ways, but one of the primary ways is through decree, through confession, through proclamation.
I quoted to you yesterday, the kingdom of God is not meat or drink, but it's righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. Righteousness, peace, and joy.
That's the realm of salvation.
Righteousness deals with the sin issue. Peace deals with the torment issue. Joy deals with the healing issue. Laughter is good medicine.
So it's a triune salvation, spirit, soul, and body.
In the Holy Spirit. So the kingdom is in the realm of the spirit.
So if the kingdom is in the realm of the spirit, what happens every time you say what God is saying?
The kingdom becomes manifest.
The kingdom Jesus never manifested the kingdom in a military sense. It wasn't a takeover. He would just proclaim what was available.
And the woman who touched the garment discovered, got access into what was available.
Have you been in a painful situation, maybe a confusion, maybe conflict, whatever you're in a situation, you're in a room maybe, maybe at a hospital, a waiting room, and everybody's anxious and nervous and somebody comes in and makes one statement and just clears the air. All of a sudden everybody just feels relieved.
What happened? Often times what happens in that moment is not just that they had a good idea, it's that they were saying something the Father was saying.
And when that takes place, what happens is the presence of God is released into the environment and the peace that conquers chaos became manifest.
Here's what we know: peace goes beyond understanding. So, if you really want the peace that passes understanding, you have to give up your right to understand.
Peace doesn't come because I comprehend. Peace comes because I surrender.
So, Jesus comes to a crowd and he begins to speak and then he makes this comment. He says, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand. Repent, change the way you think, because I brought my world with me."
And if you don't change your perspective on reality, you'll never discover what's within arms reach that you were born for, that you ache for, that you long for.
It's at hand. It's within reach. It's in here and it's now.
And so the Lord is working every day of our lives. He's working on us to change how we think and how we see reality around us.
So, the disciples in the story were being groomed to confront the obstacles to the will of God. What was the will of God? To go to the other side of the sea.
But there was something in the way, and it was a storm.
They're being groomed to carry this person into the world. We have this incredible privilege of hosting the presence of God.
The Holy Spirit is in every believer, but he doesn't rest upon every believer. And he probably rests upon all of us at different times, but for me the goal is to learn to host him continuously.
And one of the ways that I put it that can help us to understand the purpose for this is that he is in me. The Holy Spirit is in me for my sake. But he comes upon me for yours.
When the Spirit of God comes upon us, it's to alter the environment that we walk into. It's to bring transformation and change to any environment that he assigns us to.
Now, Jesus, I hear—I have prayed it myself years ago and I hear people pray, "Oh God, bind the devil for us." And last time I read he said you bind the devil.
What does it mean to bind? It means to hold him to a contract. We have a written contract that we have authority over him. So, it's a binding contract.
If you buy a car and you decide not to make payments, the bank will say we have a binding contract. You either pay us or we take the car back. We're going to hold you to the contract.
And the Scripture says you will trample on all the powers of darkness.
We bind the enemy to that contract that was written by someone superior to us.
It's nothing we've earned or deserved, but it's something we responsibly carry and walk in. So, we bind the enemy to that.
Here in this situation, Jesus is training his disciples to speak to storms, obstacles.
Remember he says to speak to the mountain, have it removed. That's an obstacle to the will of God.
How long do you keep your job if you keep asking your boss to do what he told you to do?
It becomes very easy in a lazy form of Christianity to blame the sovereignty of God for anything that doesn't happen.
And I know that I have the gift of irritation, and I irritate people when I say certain things.
But Jesus did heal everyone who came to him. And he also healed everyone the Father sent him to. There were no exceptions.
He didn't have a blind guy come to him one day and say, "Oh man, you should have been here yesterday. There was such an anointing for blindness, you know."
It's just that that never happened.
## Jesus Feeds the Multitude
All right, let's go to the next story.
The renewed mind is our internal reality becomes our reality. Number one. Number two, you can only give what you have.
He released peace because he was dwelling in peace.
Now, let's go to chapter 6 and we have another wonderful story. Let's go to verse 30.
The apostles gathered together to Jesus and told him all things, both what they had done and what they had taught.
This is interesting. I want you to make a note in your thinking to recognize how often the Scripture says what Jesus taught and what he had done. Or any other times with the apostles, what they had done, what they had taught.
And the reason I mention that is because in Western culture you could go to a business school and be taught by people who never owned a business.
Because we don't always equate, in our culture—it's just a cultural thing—we don't always equate experience with knowledge, with insight.
In fact, people pride themselves in believing something that they have no experience for.
And we are warned often, don't pursue experience.
Well, shut up.
I'm getting married, not because I believe in the theology of marriage, but because I want to live in the experience of marriage.
The kingdom of God is righteousness, peace, and joy. Two of those three realities are felt realities.
Well, brother, we're not supposed to follow signs. Signs are supposed to follow us. That's true. But if they're not following you, follow them till they follow you.
When I drive from my house to my office, I never look at the street signs because I know where I'm going.
And if we're going to go where we've never gone before, we probably will need signs to get there.
And if there are no signs on the road you're traveling on, perhaps you're not on the road you think you're on.
I should get back to my jokes. I can tell I need to get back.
So, here it says, all that Jesus began to do and teach. Luke chapter 1. "O Theophilus, this is an account of all that Jesus began to do and teach."
So, the disciples are giving a report to him because they had been sent out two by two, and they came back to tell him, this is what we said, and this is what we saw happen.
So, all of you that are Bible teachers, this is not to shame anyone, but Bible teachers prepare the soil for the miracle. You either teach to explain what just happened, or you teach to bring about the miracle.
Doesn't mean miracles have to happen in every teaching, but they need to be a continuous part of the teaching and the proclamation of the Word.
It says in John chapter 3, Nicodemus comes to Jesus and says, "We know that you are a teacher come from God because no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with them."
So, the teaching and the doing need to happen in the same culture, not always the same moment, but in the same momentum of Scripture.
The miraculous has got to happen. Why? He sent his Word and healed them.
Verse 31, he said, "Come aside by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a while." There were many coming and going. They did not even have time to eat. So, they departed to a deserted place in a boat by themselves.
But the multitude saw them departing and many knew him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.
And Jesus, when he came out, saw a great multitude, was moved with compassion for them because they were like sheep not having a shepherd. So, he began to teach them many things.
Now, when the day was far spent, his disciples came to him and said, "This is a deserted place and already the hour is late. Send them away that they may go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat."
But he answered and said to them, "You give them something to eat."
I try to imagine sometimes this setting.
They're giving Jesus a report. They go to the other side. They finally get some R&R with Jesus. They get off the boat, and the people who are on that side of the lake ran around to this side of the lake, and they're going, "Oh no, Jesus is going to do that compassion thing, and we just lost our vacation right there."
And so Jesus was moved with compassion, starts ministering to people, and after a day of that, the disciples came to Jesus.
And this is how I imagine it. Jesus, a few of us have been talking, and we like you have a great burden for these people.
And if we don't send them away, they're going to die along the way because they have not had anything to eat. So, we need to send them away.
And Jesus says, "You feed them."
And then he doesn't laugh afterwards. He doesn't go, "Ah, just kidding." He says, "You feed them."
And you can imagine the disciples are in a moment of panic because they know that he knows.
You know the rest of the story. I want you to go to the next half of this story, though.
He has them sit down. There's the great multiplication of food.
But I want you to look at verse 45 and go through this part of the story because we have something very necessary for us to learn in this part of the story.
Verse 45, "Immediately he made his disciples get into a boat and go to the other side to Bethsaida when he sent the multitude away.
"And when he sent them away, he departed to the mountain to pray. When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea. He was alone on the land.
"And he saw them straining at rowing."
This was by revelation. He couldn't see where he was standing in the natural. So, the Holy Spirit worked with Jesus to reveal, because remember he limited himself to the limitations of a human being dependent on the Father.
So, he saw them straining at rowing. The wind was against them. It was the fourth watch of the night. He came to them walking on the sea, would have passed them by.
And when they saw him walking on the sea, they supposed it was a ghost and cried out.
They all saw him. They were troubled. Immediately he talked with them and said, "Be of good cheer. It is I. Do not be afraid."
How many of you ever recognize anytime Jesus says, "Do not be afraid"? It's because you have a really good reason to be afraid.
He went up into the boat to them, and the wind ceased.
Now, here's the key for both stories.
They were greatly amazed in themselves beyond measure and marveled, for they had not understood about the loaves, because their heart was hard.
See, the miracle in one part of your life is actually to equip you for the next season.
But it wasn't about loaves. It was about the readiness of the impossibilities of life to bow to the name Jesus through our lips.
It's about us displacing darkness, replacing it with light. It's about releasing and revealing the will of God in the earth.
And so, the disciples in this story, they are told by Jesus, "Put the people in groups of 50, 100." He passed out the loaves and the fishes.
And they began to pass out the loaves and fishes. They started with a few baskets and ended up with more leftovers than they started with. It's an extraordinary story.
The part that I want you to see here, though, is that Jesus commissioned them to do a miracle.
Law requires, grace enables.
The law requires, but grace enables.
So, whenever the Lord gives a command, in the command is the ability to carry it out.
It's in what he said.
Jack Taylor, he's home with the Lord now, a great Southern Baptist teacher and pastor and revivalist, dear friend.
He talked to us once about this passage in Luke chapter 1 or 2, I forget now, where the angel speaks and says nothing will be impossible with God.
For nothing will be impossible with God.
He talked to us about the structure of the original language, and nothing, as many of you know, is two words. It's no, and it's the word rhema.
No freshly spoken Word of God will be impossible.
The word impossible actually means without ability.
So, it can be translated like this: no freshly spoken Word of God will ever come to you that does not carry its own ability to perform itself.
No freshly spoken Word of God will ever come to you that does not carry its own ability to perform itself.
You take a kernel of corn, you plant it in the ground, the soil is important, the water's important, the sunlight is important, but the ability to produce is in the seed.
And the ability for the miraculous is in the seed of his Word that he speaks into our heart. That's why quick yieldedness and surrender is so vital, so critical.
So, Jesus said to the disciples in the most impossible situation, he said, "You feed them."
And then he told them how. Set the people in groups. Then he gave them a small amount of fish, and they started handing it out.
What didn't happen, Jesus didn't take loaves and fishes, throw it in the air and go shazam and create a huge pile of food. They would have a riot on their hands.
Instead, what they did is they handed out the food, and what they noticed is that as they handed out the food, the baskets never became empty.
We've actually had that happen. We had a group in an organization, I think it was Mozambique. They had a crowd they were going to minister to and they wanted to get them bread. They got them these small loaves, and when they came back the crowd had multiplied in size and they didn't have enough.
And one of the leaders said, "You know, what do we do? Should we start breaking them up in pieces so everybody gets a bite?" And somebody else said, "No, let's each give them a loaf and see what happens."
And they did. Everybody got a loaf of bread, and when they were done, they had three bags. When they were done, two were two-thirds empty and one was half empty. They couldn't empty the bag. They just kept giving away, giving away, giving away.
Why was this important to understand what happened with the loaves for the miracle on the sea?
See, they thought if Jesus wasn't in the boat with them, they would die.
They didn't realize that when Jesus said they were to go to the other side of the sea, that Word was to enable them to go through the impossibility and to accomplish what they were assigned to do.
That story was in the loaves.
You feed them.
And because of the hardness of heart, they did not see how the miracle actually happened. Here's the real story.
The multiplying of the loaves and fishes did not happen through Jesus' hands. It happened through the disciples' hands.
Why? Because Jesus said, "You feed them."
It certainly doesn't point to our greatness. It points to the significance of hearing what God is saying.
As I stated yesterday, great faith doesn't come through great striving. It comes through great surrender.
It's yieldedness to whatever God says. It's the hearing of his voice, that tenderness of our heart that hears what he says, and we just take the courage and pursue what he says.
But in that obedience is the ability to feed a multitude that you didn't have enough food for.
And to make it through a storm that you thought you'd die in.
Because he said, "You're going to the other side."
So, the renewed mind realizes that God enables what he commands.
Remember, law requires. So, many of us try to obey God as law, the law that requires, as though we were to generate the enthusiasm, the power, the faith, whatever it is to obey what he said. When it really comes to a yieldingness in a place of surrender.
## The Leaven of the Pharisees and Herod
Go to chapter 8 and we'll wrap this up. I've got a little bit of time left, so let's see if we can make a bigger mess than we already have.
Mark chapter 8. This particular chapter has been really formative in my own life. I won't give the full story, but one of the most important chapters for me in learning how God thinks.
And I wish I could say I had it figured out, but I'm on the journey.
Verse 13.
He left them, getting into the boat again, departed to the other side.
Now, the disciples had forgotten to take bread. They did not have more than one loaf with them in the boat. Then he charged them, saying, "Take heed. Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod."
Okay, the Pharisees is the religious system. Herod is the political system.
The religious system has God at the center of everything, but he's impersonal and powerless.
The political system is humanistic. It has man at the center of everything.
So, there's three primary influences in the world, all trying to shape how we think and see.
The political system, humanism. The religious system, powerless. Form without power.
And then there's the kingdom. Matthew 13 says the kingdom of heaven is like leaven.
So, there's three leavens that are to influence the lump of dough, which is between in ears, all right? This is a lump of dough.
So, he says, "Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, that which tries to shape how you think, and the leaven of Herod."
And they reasoned among themselves, verse 16, saying, "It's because we have no bread."
I think this is so funny.
The disciples, Jesus starts talking to them about leaven, and the disciples are looking at each other and going, "Did you bring the bread?"
"I didn't bring the bread. Ask Judas, he has the money."
And so they forgot to bring food.
So, what scene did they just leave before they got into the boat?
The second time they multiplied food.
So, they just left multiplying food, got into the boat. Jesus says, "Be careful of the leaven of Herod and Pharisees."
And the guy is going, "Oh no, we brought no food."
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "It's because we have no bread."
But Jesus, being aware of it, it's like Jesus said, "All right, I wasn't talking about lunch, but let's pretend I was."
"Why do you reason because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive nor understand? Is your heart still hardened? Having eyes, do you not see? Having ears, do you not hear? Do you not remember?
"When I broke the five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up?" They said, "Twelve."
"Also, when I broke the seven for the 4,000, how many large baskets full of fragments did you take up?" They said, "Seven."
He says, "How is it you don't understand?"
See, God's math is different.
Economically, heaven was rocked by a widow's mite.
It's not amounts or sizes. It's quality. It's the completeness of an offering.
So, Jesus takes them through divine reasoning in the story. He says, "All right, when we fed the 5,000 men, not counting women and children, where did Jesus get the lunch?"
From a child, from someone who didn't count.
Jesus works differently. Everybody counts to him.
Besides women and children, on the day of Pentecost, they counted everybody, not just the men.
Because the outpouring of the spirit creates a level playing field.
So, he says, "When I broke the five loaves for the 5,000, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up?" They said, "Twelve."
Five loaves, 5,000.
"When I broke the four loaves, when I started with less and I fed more people, how many baskets full of fragments did I take up?" They said, "Seven."
"So, when you started with less, you fed more and had more leftovers?"
There's a story about George Mueller, who was one of the great heroes in the faith in church history.
The story goes something like this. He was praying, and he got a vision for a new facility that he was to build, and he was walking from his prayer room towards another part of the orphanage place.
As he was walking across the playground, a child comes up to him and hands him a penny and says, "This is for the new building."
He hadn't announced to anybody.
He took the penny, he raised it before the Lord. He said, "Thank you for the confirmation."
Now, I like confirmations of like a $100,000. Million dollars. Give me big. Give me a good confirmation.
But the eyes of faith see the potential of a small moment.
The eyes of faith see the potential. The power was in the promise. The power was in what God said was to happen.
And the more the harder my heart is, the more I need to be impressed.
If you could imagine leaving a thumbprint on something that's soft and tender, there's the fingerprint of God left with a slight touch on the tender places of our lives.
But the more I'm resistant to, you know, we sometimes fight so hard to not be gullible that we become unbelieving.
Not you, but them other people, they do it all the time.
So, if you look at this story with me, again, it says that they reasoned among themselves.
And he said, "Why do you reason because you have no bread?" I mentioned this to you yesterday, but I'll do it again.
How many of you have had a financial miracle?
How many after that miracle you had another financial problem?
How many of you were as nervous the second time as you were the first time?
So here Jesus is introducing them to a lifestyle of miracles because we're actually supposed to be trained to think different through the miracles we experience.
Now, tragically, we know enough to celebrate the miracle. We know enough to celebrate the extraordinary things that God does. We celebrate, we give him praise, we don't take the credit for ourselves. We make sure that God gets the glory for the miracle, but it doesn't always change how we think.
It helps us to include the possibility of a miracle the next time we face a problem, but it doesn't mean I necessarily think different.
Does that make sense to you? Doesn't mean I necessarily see from a different place. I once saw from down there, but now I see from here. Why? Because I experienced the miraculous supply of God.
And so once I've experienced the supernatural supply of God, I've lost my right to start any thought process with what I don't have.
Any thought process that I start with what I don't have will have to be dismantled, and I will have to repent because I have the wrong foundation. The foundation is on my resource and not his.
Why do you reason? Because you have no bread. Do you not perceive nor understand? Is your heart still hardened?
And he takes them through that story of the multiplying of loaves and fishes.
The Lord is introducing us to a kingdom that is present.
You know what I get jealous for? What Jesus walked in and what he lived in, what he—how is it that he could be so filled and overflowing with the Spirit of God that he could walk through a crowd where people are bumping him, asking him questions, talking to him, listening to every word that comes out of his mouth, and in that chaos, a woman touches him like everybody else, but this woman has faith.
And he recognizes a virtue, power flowed from him into somebody else.
I'm asking this question because I'm trying to learn this one. How do you live in the middle of chaos and recognize when somebody has put a demand on what you carry?
Now, if I'm one-on-one with somebody and I can tell they have great faith, I remember this gal. She had a medical device, a pump. She literally stayed alive. I think she had to have this medication pumped into her body every few minutes. She would die without this pump for four minutes.
And she came up, and I could see visibly, I could see the faith on her. And prayed for her. She went down on the ground, went and got up. I said, "Your faith got you this one."
She came back the next day. She took the pump off the next morning.
Which basically means I'm either healed or Jesus, I'll be here early. I'll be coming home early, but she was completely healed.
I could see, I could feel, I could recognize. I was thankful I could actually see it this time. I could see faith on her as genuine. I've heard faith a lot, but I could see that one. And it was different. It smelled different, tasted different.
One-on-one maybe, but how do you walk through a crowd and you're so in tune with the Spirit of God who rests upon you that you can tell when there's a need here and somebody's just taken a withdrawal?
Made withdrawal not because he was missing something, because he had the Spirit without measure.
So, there's this awareness of God's purposes. There's this awareness of this unseen kingdom that is more real than the seen kingdom.
Since it's more real, it's probably reasonable for me to become more conscious of that world than this one.
The Lord is introducing us to experiences. It may be a prayer that you pray where you see the miracle. It may be you're with a group of people and you see this person get out of a wheelchair.
When these things happen, do everything you can to absorb.
In fact, this gal that I just made a reference to, when she came up to me and she said, "I believe that tonight's to be my night."
Well, I've had so many people say that through the years and I just always make an agreement with them. But when she walked up and said, "Tonight's my night," I could feel it physically.
And this is actually what I did. It may have looked strange to her, but she's standing in front of me. She said, "Tonight I feel like tonight's my night."
I stepped back and I examined her from head to toe and from toe to head, but not just with my eyes. I wanted my entire person to recognize I was in the presence of extraordinary faith. I wanted something in me to recognize this because I had never seen this at this level before.
And then I went back, prayed for her, and she was healed.
But the point is to learn to recognize what it is that God is saying to him. Learn to recognize this unseen kingdom that is greater than everything that we see.
In fact, what happens in this world that's greater than the physical is it shapes this one. It molds. It redefines.
It's this unseen reality that becomes—well, I like I saw somebody say, "Water longs to be walked on again."
What a statement. I saw that in a book. Water longs to be walked on.
There's the world is aching for the manifestation of who Jesus is once again.
And you and I are on the edge of this thing constantly because you live in that kind of a lifestyle. And I don't mean this in a flattering sense. It's just you've already said yes.
You already drank the Kool-Aid. It's too late.
We've already said yes together that we believe that what Jesus said is to happen in the earth is to happen in the earth now through us, in us, through us.
So, we've already said yes to this.
So, how do we go from that conviction into the continuous realization that the promised land is unfolding before us?
I think in large part it's the renewed mind.
Let me put it this way. It is possible for you to eat food and sometimes, because of the health conditions that you may have, sometimes because the combination of foods, but it's possible for you to eat nutritious food and have it pass through you and not benefit from the nutrients.
Right?
It's possible for you to eat food and actually not benefit from the nutrients.
It happens in the church all the time. We have the food of the miraculous, but we are never nourished from what took place to the point where we think and see differently.
See, when Jesus asked them, he says, "Can't you see?" In this passage, he says, "Can you see? Can you hear? Can you remember?"
When I get those questions, tell them hello for me.
Can you see? Well, most of the time I have to say, "No, I'm not seeing very good."
Occasionally I see, but right now I'm not seeing anything but this problem.
Can you hear? Well, I hear better than I see. But maybe in that moment, God, I'm not hearing either.
Can you remember?
Now you got me.
Why? Because I equate seeing to a spiritual gift, maturity. Hearing to a spiritual gift, maturity.
Remembering is a choice.
And if I treasure what I've seen the Lord do, if I treasure the things that I've heard taking place in the earth, enough to mark them in my heart, I can recall them whenever I need to.
And what I've noticed is the more I remember, the better I hear. And the better I hear, the better I see.
The disciples are in a boat where they don't have enough food.
They just got out of an experience of multiplication of food.
Jesus is wanting them to take the lenses of that miracle to see their present situation of being without food.
In other words, your history with God is to shape how and what you see in the present.
Our experiences in the Lord. I mean they've—I feel like I'm preaching to the choir, so forgive me because I don't in any way want to take advantage of you, but for every one of us we become accustomed to certain things in the Gospel.
And one of the most fun things in the world for the people that I spend time with—I just love so much. John and Carol Arnott are just the most amazing people.
I'll sit on the front row with them, and there'll be a testimony that I know they've heard a thousand times. And they're just not jaded. They are not calloused in any way.
And I'll sit next to John, and there'll be a testimony that I know they've seen so many times. It never got old, and John'll lean over to Carol and go, "Isn't that wonderful, Carol?" And Carol go, "Oh yes, it is, John."
And I'm thinking, I need—well, hello.
I hear them and I think, "Man, I need to get saved. That's what I need."
These people have kept everything so fresh and new that the slightest things that God does leaves a mark.
It's the childlike approach, the wonder. Maintaining the awe and the wonder.
That it never becomes "been there, done that."
Never becomes, "Oh, we saw this 20 years ago." No, no, no, no. This is a new day.
You may have seen the same manifestation, but this is fresh. This is new. What God is doing, keeping that childlike tenderness of heart that just is so impressionable. I think it's vital for where he's taking us.
And the whole thing is that our history with God is to create lenses, lenses through which we see where we're going, what we're facing, the circumstances that we have in our lives.
Things are shaped by this history with God.
## The Testimony of Jesus
I'll give you one more thought. And then I'm going to end early. You know, I ended early yesterday, today this like I'm giving you a whole new recess. If we were in grade school, you'd be on the monkey bars.
In Psalms 119:111, it says the testimony of the Lord is our heritage, our inheritance forever.
Okay, so think about this.
I'll give you this concept of the testimony.
Revelation 19:10 says the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.
Testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. Say that with me. The testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.
So a testimony is either a spoken or written record of anything God has done. Would you agree with that? Spoken or written record of anything God has done.
It is the spirit of prophecy. It carries the anointing of the prophetic.
What does the prophetic do? The prophetic does one of two things generally. Number one is it foretells the future or it brings about a change in the present.
Are you with me on that? The prophetic sometimes will foretell the future, but sometimes it's a right-now word that changes circumstances in the present.
So a testimony carries the anointing to change a present reality.
It carries a prophetic anointing.
The word testimony in the Old Testament comes from a word that means to do again.
So what that means is Israel was required to study and to hold to, to memorize the commandments of the Lord, the statutes of the Lord, and the testimony.
I know what it is to keep a commandment: you do what he says. The statutes, you work for understanding on the principles that shape culture. But the third, to keep the testimony? How do you keep a testimony?
You keep it before you until it shapes how you see your present world.
And he says it's the spirit of prophecy, which means it brings about a change in the present.
So think through this with me. In Psalms 119:111, he says the testimony of the Lord is your inheritance forever, which means what? The full record of everything God has done is your personal possession.
He did not say your experience only. He said the testimony of the Lord is your possession.
## Testimony and Healing
I was in Minnesota and prayed for this girl who'd been in a snowmobile accident. She had screws and stuff in her ankle and was an associate pastor's wife.
And so I was praying for her one evening, and she got some relief, but nothing that we were looking for as far as the manifestation of God's work.
And she came to me the next morning. We had night, morning, night, morning meetings. And so, she came to me the next morning, and she said, "When I was getting dressed this morning, my husband looked down at my leg and said, 'Hey, that wasn't there before.'"
And she looked down, and the calf muscle that was missing grew back overnight.
And so, I had her give her testimony. I said, "Man, that's amazing." So, there's only like 20 or 30 people in the room for this morning session. I said, "Just tell them what happened."
So, she told the story, and as she's going back to her seat, a gal comes off the front row, comes walking up to me. She said, "If God did that for her, certainly he would do that for me."
Because she understood he's no respecter of persons, number one, and he's the same yesterday, today, and forever.
And so, I said, "Hey." So, I called the gal. I said, "Come back here." So, she came up. The pastor's wife came, and they prayed with this gal.
It had been an automobile accident many, many years ago. She had lost part of the calf muscle and had to actually relearn how to walk.
And so, they prayed for her, and they watched as the muscle grew back before their eyes.
Now, I'm going to give you—we have many, many years of this history, but I'm going to give you just one storyline, and then I promise I still have 10 minutes. I promise to wrap it up.
I will land this plane, not in the side of a hill. I'm going to land it on a runway, and we will all survive this one.
So, she comes up, and they pray for her, and they watch as that muscle forms in her leg as they pray.
Through the power of a testimony. Why? Because testimonies prophesy.
They prophesy God's nature and his intent in the now.
So, another lady comes. Two more ladies came up. They don't know it was like an epidemic of missing calf muscles and I don't know what happened, but it was like God arranged everyone in Minnesota, you know, that was missing that part of the muscle, they came up.
One of them had a big growth, a tumor there where the muscle used to be. It dissolved, the muscle grew back. The fourth one, I don't remember what happened, but she was healed as well.
So, I actually went from that town in Minnesota to a place in Tennessee. And a medical doctor came up and he had—I forget the injury. I think he had broken his leg. His muscles had atrophied.
He was really hurting. It restricted movement, pain, everything. And the muscles had atrophied, so they had shrunk in size.
And so, I had a team pray for him, and when he was—he got up and I said, "How are you doing?" He says, "I can feel the skin stretching."
As the Lord is actually replacing what had atrophied, and it was this year-long process that had happened a year ago and this was now growing back.
Why? I shared the testimony of these four women up in Minnesota. And so, he got inspired for his miracle because of the testimony.
Please understand when a testimony is given, there is the nutrients for a miracle.
It's more than to entertain us and to cheer us on. It's every testimony carries a revelation of his nature, of his covenant, and of his present-tense commitment to you and me.
That's the power of testimonies.
One more. I went from that place to be with Mahesh and Bonnie Chavda in Charlotte, North Carolina. Such great people.
And they happen to have a tent at that time. They have a building now, but they had a tent at that time.
So, I'm giving these stories because they're fresh on my mind. I'm giving these stories, these testimonies, and a gal right back over here, she yells out, "I'm missing part of my calf muscle."
Right in the middle of my message. It totally interrupted everything. It's horrible.
"I'm missing my calf muscle." And I just started to say, "Come to me at the end of the meeting and we'll pray."
And then she says, "And I'm from Minnesota."
Now, there's no magic to where you come from. But for me, that's an unusual coincidence.
And oftentimes the language of the spirit is unusual coincidence.
Unusual coincidences at minimum testify to you you're at the right place at the right time. And sometime it carries more substance.
And in essence, soon as she said, "And I'm from Minnesota." Remember in the testimony I said it started in Minnesota. She said, "I'm from Minnesota." I said, "All right." I said, "Go to the back of the tent and come and see me."
So I continued to teach. She went to the back of the tent, came up to see me. By the time she got to me, the muscle had grown back.
## Conclusion
He's teaching us how to think and how to see.
You know, people say, "Billy, you believe in miracles? Why do you wear glasses?" You know why I wear glasses? I see better with them.
And he doesn't work for me. I work for him.
Let's stand.
You know, I have the privilege to talk to people all over. And being with you guys has been such an honor for me. Just beyond words.
And I'm so thankful. And what happens in my heart, if you can imagine, is I become provoked with you by the invitation of the Lord to think different. To see different.
And so I think it'd be good if we just took a moment just to pray.
In fact, why don't you do this? Let's do this just in a little weird way. Just put your hand on the shoulder of someone next to you.
And just, in fact, look at them and say, "I hope you were listening."
Because he was talking right to you.
Now, here's what I want you to do. I want you to pray that God would overwhelm them in giving them insight on how to think, how to see, how to release the kingdom.
Put it in your own words. But, let's take like two minutes. Just pray for one another. And pray that the Spirit of God would come upon them in a profound way.
Thank you, Lord. Increase, increase, increase.
Thank you, Lord.
Father, we ask that you would lead us into the encounters that transform our thinking.
That we would receive the nutrients of every story we hear.
Help us to put on display your wonderful will for planet Earth.
Our cry is that we represent you well, and we give you thanks. We give you praise.
Everybody said, "Amen." Amen. Bless you.

# The Truth Is Not Out There
*Study Blog Edition*
**Speaker:** Pastor Michael Paul Varghese **Source:** [Word of His Grace Broadcast](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XyHTwSipLLM) **Date:** August 26, 2026
---
## The Great Shepherd of the Sheep
Praise the Lord Jesus. We are here again by His grace for another Wednesday of meditation in the Word of God, our weekly Bible study. We worship Him who is worthy. We give Him thanks and praise: the invisible God, the Holy One of Israel. We worship the Father and give thanks for the Holy Spirit who lives in us. We ask Him to unveil Jesus to us.
We are grateful that Jesus is at the right hand of the Majesty on high, pleading and interceding for us. We are grateful for the privilege of taking our place as His body on the earth. To Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing, glory, honor, and power forever.
Hebrews 13:20-21 gives us a prayer that says, in part, that the God of peace brought again from the dead our Lord Jesus, that great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant, and that He would make us mature in every good work to do His will, working in us what is well pleasing in His sight through Jesus Christ.
There is a wonderful picture here. Jesus was the Lamb led to the slaughter. He was silent before His shearers. He laid down His life for the sheep. After His resurrection, He became the great Shepherd of the sheep. Through the covenant blood that He Himself shed, He is now committed to perfect that which concerns us.
He is doing His part, pleading for us and working in us what is well pleasing in His sight. All of this is in Christ, who has given us the privilege of being in Him. To Him be glory and honor forever and ever.
Some things are eternal and some things are temporary. Jesus has passed into the eternal realm, and He can faithfully undertake for us, watchfully and prayerfully keeping us. We look to His goodness and mercy.
## Truth Has More Than One Side
Every now and then, we look for Scriptures that minister peace and quietness to our souls. John 3:16 is one of those Scriptures: God loved the world and gave His only begotten Son so that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. It is filled with goodness and mercy.
But there are other verses that are true even though they are not as comfortable to hear. John 3:35-36 says that the Father loves the Son and has given all things into His hand. Whoever believes in the Son has everlasting life, but whoever does not believe the Son shall not see life, and the wrath of God remains on him.
That is not a verse that people naturally want to display everywhere. Yet it is true. There are different sides to the multifaceted wisdom of God. He is the only wise God, and some things about Him are simply the way He is.
There is a strong drive toward universal acceptance in a sinful world. We should appeal to people by every means possible through the precious blood of Jesus. Yet there is also a serious truth: if people do not choose the mercy of God in this life, they will face consequences. This is the best time to accept the wonderful mercy of God.
Jesus is both the Lamb and our propitiation. The Lamb is gentle, kind, merciful, and precious. He takes away the sin of the world. Propitiation means that the wrath of God against sin was satisfied through the sacrifice of Jesus. God hates sin and everything that is evil. Jesus came and bore the judgment that sin deserved.
If a person does not accept the mercy offered in the Lamb's blood, the wrath that Jesus bore remains something that person must face. Jesus became the propitiation, the satisfactory sacrifice, and He bore the wrath of God against sin.
These truths must be received together. We cannot understand the compassionate Lamb while rejecting the holiness of God. We need both sides or we will paint the wrong picture of the One we are dealing with.
## Jesus Our Advocate and Propitiation
First John 2:1-2 says that John writes to believers so that they do not sin. Yet, if anyone does sin, we have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous. He is our Advocate with the Father.
An advocate is someone called to defend you. In the heavenly court of God, the righteous Judge, we have someone to call upon who will defend us. Every believer has Jesus Christ the righteous as an Advocate.
John then says that Jesus is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world. The word translated propitiation is connected with the idea of the mercy seat. In the Old Testament tabernacle, the blood of the sacrifice was applied at the mercy seat. The sacrifice dealt with sin before God.
Today Jesus becomes our mercy seat, and His blood is our mercy. He is the appropriate sacrifice, the sacrifice that satisfies the holiness and justice of God.
This sacrifice was not only for believers. Jesus offered Himself for the sins of the whole world. Believers have accepted what He has done. The rest of the world is still being called to receive it. Jesus has provided the sacrifice, but people must respond to the mercy offered to them.
Therefore, today is the day and now is the hour to take advantage of what this precious Lamb has done. We have an Advocate who pleads for us and speaks on our behalf with the Father, the righteous Judge of the whole earth.
## Love That Begins With God
First John 4:10 says that love is not first defined by our love for God. It says that He loved us and sent His Son to be the propitiation for our sins. The sacrifice was offered first. We did not know about it or earn it. He first loved us and gave Himself for us.
The world has little idea about this. We owe it to people to explain and offer this wonderful mercy to them.
The next verse says that because God so loved us, we ought also to love one another. God's love now affects how we walk on this earth.
Psalm 23 speaks about walking through the valley of the shadow of death. It is not only death itself, but the shadow of death. There are thoughts and ideas that come against the mind and imagination. Fear can enter the mind even when the feared thing is not the reality.
A shadow is not the reality. The reality is that we have the life of God. The reality is that God loves us. The reality is that Jesus is pleading for us. The reality is that we share His life. Everything else is a shadow.
Yet shadows can still interfere with clear thinking. Therefore, we must make an effort to think on what is true. We have to learn to think life in the midst of shadows of death all around us.
## The Revelation of Jesus Christ
John also wrote the book of Revelation. Revelation 1:1 calls it the revelation of Jesus Christ. It is not merely the revelation of John. God gave the revelation to Jesus Christ to show His servants the things that must shortly come to pass, and Jesus signified it through His angel to His servant John.
Revelation 1:3 says, "Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand."
If the time was described as being at hand two thousand years ago, then we should recognize how close the fulfillment appears to be now. There is a blessing attached to reading, hearing, and keeping these words.
Reading Scripture should not be treated as a private intellectual exercise only. In the original setting, reading often meant proclaiming the words aloud to a gathered community. We should give the Word a voice. Read it and say it.
As we continue through Revelation, we notice that one of the main figures is the Lamb. The Lamb is repeatedly magnified in the book. Jesus is presented through the character of the Lamb: gentle, merciful, innocent, and lovable.
Then Revelation also shows the Lamb in another aspect. The church is pictured as having been gathered to Christ, and the marriage of the Lamb becomes a central image. Revelation 19 speaks of the marriage of the Lamb and says that His wife has made herself ready. The fine linen represents the righteous deeds of the saints.
There is an amazing picture here for our imagination. The same Lamb who is gentle and merciful is also the holy Judge of sin.
## The Wrath of the Lamb
Revelation 6:12-17 describes the opening of the sixth seal. John sees a great earthquake, the sun becoming black as sackcloth, the moon becoming like blood, stars falling to the earth, the heavens departing as a scroll, and mountains and islands being moved out of their places.
John is recording what he saw. He is not simply adding his own interpretation. He reports the events as he witnessed them.
Then the kings of the earth, great men, rich men, chief captains, mighty men, bondmen, and free men hide themselves in the dens and rocks of the mountains. They say to the mountains and rocks, "Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb."
Notice the words: the wrath of the Lamb.
The Lamb is not only tender. The Lamb also has wrath. Revelation 6:17 says that the great day of His wrath has come, and asks who shall be able to stand.
These are not abstract future ideas that have no connection with human choice. The message is that people need to respond while mercy is available. We should not minister these truths with a desire to condemn anyone. We should set forth the truth.
There is a reality of judgment. There is also a present opportunity for mercy. Jesus has taken the wrath for those who receive Him. We should therefore offer the Gospel of reconciliation without fear.
## Do Not Be Uncomfortable With Truth
We should not become uncomfortable when we hear truth. We should make adjustments. We may squirm when the truth confronts us, but we need a steady diet of truth because we are constantly bombarded by lies and shadows of fear and death.
The church should be one place where truth is available. If someone wants to hear the truth, it should be available in the house of God.
We may have listened to lies, absorbed fear, or spent too much time looking at the shadows around us. The answer is not to avoid truth. The answer is to return to truth.
As we read and study the book of Revelation, we can do so with confidence in Christ. We are not reading it merely to satisfy curiosity. We are being reminded of the seriousness of the choices people make and the mercy that is available now.
We should be grateful for the grace of God and for the privilege of knowing that the Lamb has offered Himself. Our response should be to stand on the right side of this truth and continue to offer God's mercy to the world.
## Wisdom Is the Principal Thing
Proverbs 4:7 says, "Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom: and with all thy getting get understanding."
It continues by saying that when wisdom is embraced, it brings honor. This aligns with Proverbs 3, where we are told not to trust in the Lord with part of our heart, but with all our heart. We are also told not to lean on our own understanding.
God's wisdom teaches us how to make the right choices. His correction is part of His love. Wisdom is described as more valuable than silver, gold, or anything else that can be desired.
The people who seem rich and powerful but reject the mercy of the Lamb cannot finally escape the consequences of rejecting God's wisdom. We are warned in advance, so we have the ability to choose now in view of the future.
Wisdom is described as more precious than rubies. Length of days is in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and honor. She is a tree of life to those who hold her.
What do we need first? Not merely riches, honor, or long life. We need wisdom. These other things are presented as consequences of walking in wisdom.
Jesus is the embodiment of that wisdom. He is the wisdom of God. When we understand Him, these other things can become our portion in the right way. We can live from a place of rest rather than constantly chasing the things the world tells us to chase.
## The Wisdom of Humility
James 3 addresses the tongue and the inconsistency of blessing and cursing from the same mouth. A fountain cannot produce both sweet water and bitter water. A fig tree cannot produce olives, and a vine cannot produce figs.
The point is that our speech should reveal the nature of the wisdom by which we live.
We should choose to be a blessing. Our tongues should produce what strengthens and builds others up. We should separate our speech from bitterness and use it for things that are fruitful and helpful.
James 3:13 asks who is wise and endued with knowledge and says that such a person should show by good conduct and works the meekness of wisdom.
The wisdom of God is humble. The world has another kind of wisdom that is driven by pride, competition, striving, envy, and self-promotion.
There is always a temptation to be proud and to make ourselves the center. The wisdom of God is the opposite. It is a humble kind of wisdom. We choose the low road rather than insisting that we must be the highest person in the room.
This can be difficult because the world keeps reminding us that being low means being insignificant. Yet we are in good company when we walk humbly because that is how our King walked.
## Meekness Is Not Weakness
Matthew 11:25-30 shows Jesus thanking the Father because certain things are hidden from the wise and prudent in the world's sense and revealed to those who come as babes.
This does not mean that God opposes true wisdom. It means that worldly wisdom, worldly status, and worldly pride do not give a person access to the things of God.
Jesus then says that all things are delivered to Him by the Father and that no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son reveals Him. Therefore, we should interpret the Father through the Son. Jesus unveils the Father to us.
Then Jesus gives the invitation: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest."
There is a progression here. The burdened sinner comes to Jesus and finds rest. Then the disciple takes the yoke of Jesus and learns from Him. Jesus says that He is meek and lowly in heart.
That is where true wisdom is found: in meekness and lowliness.
Meekness is not weakness. It is power under control. It is strength governed by the right master. We are learning to bring our hearts under His control rather than simply doing whatever our own impulses demand.
The result is rest for the soul. The soul must be trained to find rest in what Jesus calls good instead of waiting for worldly conditions to become perfect before it can rest.
We are different because we have decided that if this is what Jesus wants, then this is what we want. His yoke is easy and His burden is light.
Therefore, our targets cannot be the same as the world's targets. We want the rest that comes from choosing what Jesus calls good.
## Get Wisdom, Not More Fear
Proverbs 3 and James 3 point us toward the same conclusion. We need wisdom, not a constant obsession with spiritual threats.
The Scripture says that the wise person is humble. Wisdom produces the ability to respect authority, honor those whom God says to honor, and live with the right priorities.
It does not make sense to think according to the world and then expect God's wisdom to function the same way. God's wisdom is hidden from pride and revealed to those who are willing to be lowly and teachable.
A basic question for self-examination is this: Have I been having a difficult time with humility?
All of us face that temptation. There is a part of human nature that wants to be the head on its own. Genesis shows this desire when people wanted to make a name for themselves. God later told Abraham that He would make Abraham's name great.
The difference is crucial. We should not force our own greatness. We should let God establish what He wants, in His timing and through His process.
That may require waiting. It may be difficult for the flesh. Yet God's Word will come to pass. He cannot forget what He has said. He remembers His covenant, His Word, and His promises.
## Two Kinds of Wisdom
James 3:14-18 gives a direct contrast between earthly wisdom and wisdom from above.
Where there is bitter envy and strife in the heart, we are told not to boast and not to lie against the truth. This kind of wisdom does not come from above. It is earthly, sensual, and devilish.
Where envy and strife exist, there is confusion and every evil work.
By contrast, the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, and easy to be entreated. It is full of mercy and good fruits. It is without partiality and without hypocrisy.
This gives us a practical picture of wisdom.
Are we pure in what we are thinking about? Are we peaceable? Are we gentle? Are we easy to live with? Are we full of mercy? Are we producing good fruit? Are we free from partiality and hypocrisy?
The target is to be like Jesus. People may disappoint us or let us down, but that does not change the target. We can still follow Jesus.
Wisdom is not merely asking God for a shortcut in a difficult situation. Wisdom means learning to think like Him and becoming like Him.
## Mercy Is the Knowledge of God
Hosea 6:6 says, "I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings."
Mercy is connected with the knowledge of God. Jesus used this Scripture Himself and told people to go and learn what it means.
Matthew 9:13 says, "Go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice."
Jesus was teaching people to study the Bible. He was not asking for religious activity without understanding. He wanted people to learn the meaning of the Scriptures.
Imagine Jesus saying to us, "Go and find out what this means. Go study these things. Learn these things."
That is why Bible study matters. People may say, "You are always talking about the Bible. You are always studying the Bible." The answer is that Jesus wants us to know what His Word means.
We can study physics, chemistry, biology, and many other subjects. Those studies have their place. But we must not forget to study the Word of God and understand its meaning.
Jesus is the Word made flesh. To know His Word is to learn His ways and understand His heart.
## What Does the Lord Require?
Micah 6:8 gives another clear statement: God has shown us what is good and what He requires. We are to do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly with our God.
Notice the connection.
We are to be full of mercy. We are to love mercy. We are to walk humbly. The meekness of wisdom is not a separate idea. These truths belong together.
We can examine our lives and ask whether we have been affected by a desire to be high and mighty, force our way through, or become self-made people.
Instead, we should let God lift up our heads. We should let Him establish His goodness in His work.
## Paul Serves With Humility
Acts 20 gives us a real example in the life of the apostle Paul. Paul was coming toward the end of his ministry and was on his way to Jerusalem.
Earlier, in Troas, a young man named Eutychus fell from the third story while Paul was preaching late into the night. Paul went down, embraced him, and the young man was found alive.
After that, Paul traveled and eventually came to Miletus, where he sent for the elders of the church at Ephesus. He wanted to speak to the church leaders.
There was an order to this. Paul did not simply address everyone in an undefined way. He called the elders, the pastors, those who had oversight.
Acts 20:18-20 begins Paul's farewell message. He reminds them how he had been with them through all seasons and says that he served the Lord with all humility of mind, with many tears and temptations.
Life is full of seasons. There are good seasons, difficult seasons, happy seasons, sad seasons, and challenging seasons. Paul says that in all those seasons he served the Lord with humility.
Some experiences are painful. We learn the true nature of people through different seasons, and those discoveries can hurt. Yet Paul kept serving in humility.
He did not hold back anything that was profitable to the people. He taught publicly and from house to house. He continued to give what would benefit them.
Paul testified to Jews and Greeks of repentance toward God and faith toward our Lord Jesus Christ.
He knew that trouble awaited him. The Holy Spirit warned him that bonds and afflictions were ahead. Yet Paul said that none of these things moved him.
Acts 20:24 captures his attitude: he did not count his life dear to himself so that he might finish his course with joy and the ministry he received from the Lord Jesus, to testify of the Gospel of the grace of God.
That is the goal: finish the course with joy.
## Do Not Hold Back What Is Profitable
Paul tells the elders that they will see his face no more. He says that he is pure from the blood of all because he did not shrink from declaring the whole counsel of God.
There is a serious responsibility in ministry. If we hold back what is profitable, we carry responsibility for what we failed to say. But if we faithfully release what God has given for the people's profit, the responsibility for their response rests with them.
Paul then tells the leaders to take heed to themselves and to all the flock over which the Holy Spirit has made them overseers. They are to feed the church of God, which He purchased with His own blood.
The church belongs to Jesus. The flock belongs to Him. Leaders have been entrusted with the responsibility of feeding and overseeing what He owns.
Paul warns that grievous wolves will enter and that even from among the church people will arise speaking perverse things to draw disciples after themselves. Divisions and unhealthy attempts to build personal followings are real dangers.
Therefore, leaders must watch and remember that Paul warned the believers continually, night and day, with tears.
There is nothing wrong with repeating a warning when you care for people. Repetition can be an expression of love when the purpose is to protect the flock.
## The Word of Grace Builds Us Up
Acts 20:32 says, "And now, brethren, I commend you to God, and to the word of his grace, which is able to build you up, and to give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified."
Paul did not covet anyone's silver, gold, or clothing. He did not look at someone's possessions and desire to have them. He worked with his own hands.
His ministry was not driven by personal gain. He was concerned about the profit of the people and the fulfillment of the calling he had received.
After he had said these things, Paul knelt down and prayed with them. They wept openly, embraced him, and were especially sorrowful because they would see his face no more.
There was a real relationship between Paul and the churches. He was not remote from them. He wanted to see them face to face.
The Christian life in Scripture is not designed as an isolated existence. The church is a people who see one another, know one another, care for one another, and walk together through different seasons.
## You Are Part of the Body
There is something important about seeing the faces of people and developing real affection for them. Scripture does not present the Christian life as a robot-like experience in which everyone lives as an isolated individual.
You are not the whole church by yourself. You are part of the church. You are one small stone in the larger structure of the body of Christ. You are one piece in something much bigger than yourself.
Jesus has His own plan, His own arrangement, and His own administration in His Word. We must adhere to that arrangement.
It takes humility. It takes merciful service to the Lord through many seasons, changes, disappointments, and challenges.
## Love Truth and Offer Wisdom
We must continue to love truth and desire truth. The church should be a place where wisdom and truth are offered.
God desires that our tongues and voices minister wisdom rather than envy, strife, and division.
The central target remains the same: be like Jesus. Be pure. Be peaceable. Be gentle. Be easy to live with. Be full of mercy. Produce good fruit. Walk humbly with God.
One day we will meet the Lamb Himself as His bride. The seriousness of that future meeting should make us value the mercy we have received and the truth we have been given.
First Timothy 3:15 says that if Paul is delayed, believers should know how to behave in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
Notice the phrase: the house of God. It is a house. It is a gathering. It is a place where truth is available. There is an order and an obligation in how we behave in the house of God.
The church is meant to preserve and proclaim truth.
## Conclusion
We should continue to meditate on these things.
God is good. God is loving. God is merciful. The Lamb is pleading now. We should take advantage of this age of mercy and not become casual about it.
We need wisdom. Wisdom is the principal thing. We need the meekness of wisdom. We need to love mercy, walk humbly with God, speak words that build others up, and refuse envy, strife, and division.
We should remain willing to hear truth even when it requires adjustment. The world is filled with lies and shadows. The church must be a place where the truth is available.
We should hold nothing back that is profitable. We should serve the Lord with humility through every season. We should care for the flock that belongs to Him. We should be committed to the Word of His grace, which is able to build us up.
May we be able to offer life, wisdom, and truth as we live on this earth. May we run our race and finish the purpose for which we were created. May none of us leave the earth without accurately arranging and adjusting our lives according to the wisdom of God.
We trust Him and receive these things in Jesus' name. Amen.

Is my speech producing sweet water or bitter water?

Am I learning to find rest in the meek and lowly way of Jesus?
